recipes.name: Run 1
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log
Length along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face
Length along the bark corner of the ripped face
Length along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 70.53 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the bark corner of the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 5.64 in along the point, down to 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 59.49 in along the point; 69.78 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 64.58 in along the bark corner of the ripped face; 63.74 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the ripped face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 6.86 in along the point, down to 1.72 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 69.78 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 64.58 in along the bark corner of the ripped face, 63.74 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, 59.49 in along the point. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: on a sawn face against the flat side, point back toward the wall.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).

28 ends: mitre 34.4°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the short edge
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.
Slats tilted 45°, lapped 0.50 in in plan: no straight line of sight through, but 0.03 in of clear air between each pair.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
34 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.
Slats tilted 45°, lapped 0.50 in in plan: no straight line of sight through, but 0.03 in of clear air between each pair.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
